Fit and predict

LinearRegression fits an intercept and coefficients by ordinary least squares. Predictions use the same feature columns in the same order. Coefficients alone do not establish a causal effect.

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

model = LinearRegression().fit([[1], [2], [3]], [3, 5, 7])
print(round(float(model.predict([[4]])[0]), 2))
Example output
9.0

Choose MAE, RMSE, or R²

MAE is the average absolute error and has the target’s units. RMSE gives greater weight to large errors and has the same units. R² describes performance relative to the mean-target baseline in the evaluation set and can be negative.

from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error

actual = [100, 200, 300]
predicted = [90, 210, 320]
print(round(mean_absolute_error(actual, predicted), 2))
Example output
13.33
